newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita CEO says dividend for '96 possible.
newsitem.headline: Merita CEO says dividend for '96 possible.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy will be able to pay dividend to shareholders on its 1996 earnings, chief executive Vesa Vainio said in business monthly Paakaupunkiseudun Talousuutiset received on Monday.
"We are achieving such earnings that the annual general meeting will have the possibility to decide on dividend payment," Vainio was quoted as saying in an interview.
Merita will publish its 1996 earnings on February 12.
In the January-September financial statement released on November 7, Merita said: "It is our aim that the result for 1996 will permit us to resume payment of dividend."
"B shares carry preferential rights in this respect, but we believe it will be possible to declare a modest dividend also on A shares," Merita said at the time.
In the interview, Vainio said dividend payment was "very important".
Of the two banking groups that established Merita in 1995, Unitas last paid a dividend on its 1991 earnings and Kansallis-Osake-Pankki on its 1990 earnings.
